label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Across all three psychological distress measures, this group scores notably higher than typical respondents, with anxiety symptoms being the most pronounced (mean GAD-7 item score of 2.27). The co-occurrence of heavy social-media engagement and heightened emotional distress is a defining characteristic of this cluster.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 3.9 hours with a substantial proportion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness as measured by UCLA-8 (mean item score ~1.78)
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology on PHQ-9 (mean item score ~1.81)
Highest anxiety levels among profiles on GAD-7 (mean item score ~2.27)
Pattern of co-occurring psychological distress across loneliness, depression, and anxiety dimensions
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of digital overuse and significant emotional burden

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education who report lower loneliness, lower depressive symptoms, and lower anxiety compared to other groups. They engage in relatively light daily social media use, averaging roughly 1–3 hours. Their psychological well-being indicators are consistently favorable, with notably low anxiety scores and modest depression scores, suggesting a generally stable and socially connected disposition.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social media consumption (approximately 2.8 hours midpoint)
Low self-reported loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27)
Very low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03)
Higher educational attainment (graduate level or above)
tone: Calm, stable, and psychologically resilient with a measured approach to social media engagement

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who report elevated loneliness yet comparatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms, while spending nearly five hours per day on social media. Their loneliness scores stand above average, suggesting persistent feelings of social disconnection, but these do not translate into proportionally high depression or anxiety. Their heavy daily social-media engagement may serve as a compensatory social outlet or may itself contribute to their sense of isolation despite low clinical distress.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, approximately 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate feelings of social disconnection
Lower depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90) relative to loneliness level
Lower anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85) suggesting limited clinical anxiety burden
Heavy daily social-media use averaging approximately 4.9 hours
Possible reliance on social media as a primary channel for social connection
tone: Quietly disconnected; socially active online yet personally isolated, without overt emotional distress

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents a relatively large group (n=217) of male respondents with graduate-level education who report low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their daily social-media use is light, averaging roughly 1.6 hours per day (within the 1–3 hour range). Across all psychological well-being indicators, this group scores well below scale midpoints, suggesting generally positive mental health and moderate digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media usage averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.22, well below scale midpoint)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.82)
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.90)
Pattern consistent with balanced digital habits and strong psychosocial functioning
